fixes.explanation: Yes, friend. The sisters approach the entrance to the Tent of Meeting and stand before Moses, Eleazar the priest, the leaders, and the whole congregation (Numbers 27:2). Then they speak up and make their case. Five sisters, one entrance, and a whole congregation to hear it. I respect that a whole lot.

The Jordan is a river, and it's a good guess, but the sisters never go there in this passage. They approach the entrance to the Tent of Meeting and stand before Moses, Eleazar the priest, the leaders, and the whole congregation (Numbers 27:2). If you tried to make your case by a river, friend, you'd mostly be talking to the water.

Manasseh is the ancestor of their clans, so I see why you picked it. The sisters belong to the clans of Manasseh son of Joseph (Numbers 27:1). But the text sends them to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, where they stand before Moses, Eleazar the priest, the leaders, and the whole congregation (Numbers 27:2). That's a big audience for five sisters.

Not quite, friend. The sisters say the opposite: their father "…was not among the followers of Korah who gathered together against the LORD." (Numbers 27:3). Korah led a rebellion (Numbers 16:1-3), and the sisters say their dad was not part of it. Then they add that he died because of his own sin, and they say that plainly too.

A seat sounds fancy, but that's not what they ask for. They say, "Give us property among our father’s brothers." (Numbers 27:4). Their request is about property and their father's name, not a title. I think they came with a plan, and the plan had a very short list.

Yes, friend. "…Moses brought their case before the LORD…" (Numbers 27:5). Five sisters had just made their request, and Moses took it to the LORD. I think that's the right move when a question is that big. The LORD answers him in the very next verse (Numbers 27:6).
The LORD says the opposite. His words to Moses are, "The daughters of Zelophehad speak correctly." (Numbers 27:7). He doesn't say they're mistaken. He says they have it right.

Yes, friend. The LORD says to give them property "…and transfer their father’s inheritance to them." (Numbers 27:7). That's what the sisters came asking for. Their father's inheritance goes to his daughters, right there among their father's brothers.

Debts, ha! Nobody wants those in the cookie box. But they're not in this verse. The LORD says to transfer their father's inheritance to them (Numbers 27:7). That's something given to the sisters, not a bill.

Duties are a good-sounding word, but the verse says something else. The LORD tells Moses to "…transfer their father’s inheritance to them." (Numbers 27:7). It's an inheritance they receive, along with property among their father's brothers. Nobody handed these five a to-do list.

That's it. "If a man dies and leaves no son, you are to transfer his inheritance to his daughter." (Numbers 27:8). That's the answer the five sisters walked in hoping for. Now the LORD tells Moses to say it to all the Israelites as a rule.

Right on. "If he has no daughter, give his inheritance to his brothers." (Numbers 27:9). The LORD takes it one step at a time, like a very organized recipe. Son first, then daughter, then brothers. And He's not done, because there's more to the list.

Correct. When there are no children, no brothers, and no brothers of the father, the LORD says, "…give his inheritance to the next of kin from his clan…" (Numbers 27:11). It stays in the clan, not with another tribe. That's the last step in the list the LORD gives.
